newsitem.title: JORDAN: Middle East violence hit Jordan's 1996 tourism.
newsitem.headline: Middle East violence hit Jordan's 1996 tourism.

text.p: Renewed violence in the Middle East thwarted an expected tourist boom in Jordan last year, Tourism Minister Saleh Irsheidat said on Tuesday.

Irsheidat, quoted by the official Petra news agency, said Jordan registered a disappointing 2.6 percent increase in tourists coming to Jordan in 1996. Forecasts early in the year had predicted a rise of 17 percent, he said.

Irsheidat cited a series of blows to Middle East peace in 1996 including Israel's "Grapes of Wrath" bombardment of Lebanon and violent Palestinian protests after Israel opened a tunnel exit near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem.
Jordan was also hit by riots in August after the government cut bread price subsidies.

Irsheidat said tourist revenue, a crucial source of foreign currency earnings, stood at 770 million dinars ($1.09 billion) in 1996, Petra reported. He said tourist numbers rose to 1.102 million from 1.074 million the year before.
But he said Jordan, banking on continued rises in tourism numbers, planned to almost double the number of hotel beds to 18,000 by the year 2000 from 9,400 last year.

Asked about preparations for tourists coming to celebrate the dawn of the new millennium in three years' time, Irsheidat said Jordan and Israel were coordinating plans for an expected regional influx of 15 million tourists.
